custody_model: Product-specific centralized yield arrangement. Current Earn terms state the user transfers and locks eligible cryptoassets in favor of Bit2Me and authorizes Bit2Me to transfer, dispose of or use those assets during the Earn period. This treatment is distinct from ordinary wallet custody and can include proof-of-stake activity for eligible assets under separate Earn terms.
yield_source: Variable rewards generated through Bit2Me Earn mechanisms described in current first-party material, including staking-validation rewards for eligible proof-of-stake assets and other product-supported yield activity. Reward conditions are variable and product/asset dependent.
risk_notes: Risks include Bit2Me/platform exposure created by the Earn-specific transfer/use rights, changes to reward rates and supported assets, withdrawal or suspension conditions, staking/protocol risks for applicable assets, market volatility, operational risk and regulatory change. The product is not treated as customer-owned custody while assets are subject to the reviewed Earn transfer/use terms.

custody_model: Product-specific lending/yield arrangement through the Yield Account and Coinmerce Earn B.V. Current terms define the client as lender and Coinmerce Earn as borrower; assets dedicated to Earn leave the ordinary Foundation custody structure and may be used by Coinmerce Earn for on-lending or staking with third parties.
yield_source: Yield generated by Coinmerce Earn through use of borrowed eligible assets, including on-lending and staking with third parties, with rewards credited under the current Earn/Yield Account terms. Reward levels and eligible assets are terms- and product-dependent.
risk_notes: Risks include borrower/counterparty exposure to Coinmerce Earn, third-party on-lending and staking risk, changes to reward conditions, loss of ordinary Foundation-custody treatment for dedicated Earn assets, market and liquidity risk, operational risk and regulatory change. Ordinary Coinmerce custody protections must not be generalized to the Earn lending arrangement.
